extracted.intended_audience: SBIR/STTR participating federal agencies, program managers, SBA staff, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and statutory reporting requirements for Participating Agencies under the SBIR/STTR programs, including required accounting, metrics, priorities (manufacturing, energy), and special authorities (CRPP, Direct to Phase II, Phase 0). Intended to direct agency reporting and program implementation for the FY22 Annual Report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization Readiness Pilot Program (CRPP) reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Section 9 of the Act, 15 U.S.C. § 638(b)(7)(F), participating Agencies must provide an accounting of funds, initiatives, and outcomes under the CRPP to SBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must summarize CRPP activities (funds obligated, number of awards, initiatives, outcomes) to SBA; examples of acceptable reporting include the agency-specific summaries and project success descriptions (e.g., HHS, NASA, DHS sampled success stories and amounts obligated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on awards to SBCs majority-owned by VCOCs/HFs/PEFs (portfolio companies)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reauthorization Act authorized agencies to use program funds for awards to firms majority-owned by multiple venture capital operating companies, hedge funds, or private equity firms; agencies must report such awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should include metrics such as number of proposals received, number of awards, total dollar amounts, breakdowns by Phase I/Phase II (proposals, awards, dollar amounts), number and dollar amount of non-competing Phase II awards, overall dollar amount of competing and non-competing awards, and Phase III appeals. Agencies that used the authority should supply tables like the one shown for HHS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification before pursuing follow-on (Phase III) work with third parties; Phase III appeals process
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to section 4(c)(8) of the SBIR/STTR Policy Directive, Participating Agencies are to notify the SBA before they pursue follow-on work on a technology developed under an SBIR/STTR Award with an entity other than the SBIR/STTR Awardee that developed the technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If awardees perceive violations of Phase III preference or SBIR/STTR data rights, they may contact SBA; SBA will work with the awardee and relevant agency to resolve issues and may appeal an agency decision to pursue Phase III work with another entity. Annual reporting should state whether any such notifications or appeals occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on outreach and awards to women-, socially and economically disadvantaged SBCs, and underrepresented states
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 15 U.S.C. §638(b)(7)(C), the SBA reports the extent to which each federal agency is increasing outreach and awards to firms owned and controlled by women or by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals under each of the SBIR and STTR Programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency Annual Reports should include descriptive information and statistical proposal/award data (see Sections 5 and 6) and more detailed agency activities (Section 12). Examples of outreach activities and metrics illustrating participation by these groups should be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participating Agency compliance with Executive Order 13329 (Encouraging Innovation in Manufacturing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 9(ss) of the Act, 15 U.S.C. § 638(ss), requires the Annual Report contain: a description of efforts undertaken by the head of the federal agency to enhance U.S. manufacturing activities; a comprehensive description of actions taken each year by the head of the agency in carrying out the SBIR/STTR Program in support of E.O. 13329; an assessment of the effectiveness of those actions; a description of efforts by vendors selected to provide discretionary technical assistance to help SBIR/STTR concerns manufacture in the U.S.; and recommendations for additional actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must give priority to small business concerns participating in manufacturing-related R/R&D. Mechanisms commonly used include: adding manufacturing-related topics in solicitations; requesting proposals address manufacturing-related elements of technological approach, delivery, or applicability; noting that including such elements may provide a competitive advantage; cross-agency collaborations; targeted outreach; and other agency-specific activities. Agencies making more than $50M in awards must include the above descriptions in their Annual Reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participating Agency compliance with the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007 (EISA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 9(z) of the Act, 15 U.S.C. §638(z), requires the Annual Report to include a determination of whether Participating Agencies give high priority to small business concerns that participate in or conduct energy efficiency or renewable energy system R/R&D projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should document examples of SBIR/STTR projects related to energy efficiency or renewable energy; procedures and mechanisms used during the reporting fiscal year to give priority to such projects (e.g., adding energy-related topics, asking proposals to address energy aspects); specific actions taken to promote and support energy efficiency and renewable energy research projects; and collective achievements across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual program metrics requirement under 15 U.S.C. §638(nn)
rubrics_metrics.description: The head of each Federal agency required to participate in the SBIR or STTR Program shall develop metrics to evaluate the effectiveness and the benefit to the people of the United States of the SBIR and STTR Programs of the Federal agency that are science-based and statistically driven; reflect the mission of the Federal agency; and include factors relating to the economic impact of the programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must conduct an annual evaluation using these metrics and provide that report to the House and Senate Small Business Committees, House Committee on Science, Space and Technology, and the SBA Administrator. Reports should be science-based, statistically driven, mission-reflective, and include economic-impact factors. (Note: agencies in FY22 reported that the SBA Annual Report met the spirit of this provision and no individual reports were submitted.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct to Phase II award determination and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reauthorization Act granted NIH, DoD, and ED authority to make Phase II awards without regard to whether the company received a Phase I award; prior to such an award, the head of the agency or designee must issue a written determination that the small business has demonstrated the scientific and technical merit and feasibility of the ideas that appear to have commercial potential, and submit the determination to SBA prior to issuing the Phase II award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies exercising Direct to Phase II authority must document and report the written determinations to SBA. Annual reporting should include metrics such as number of new Direct to Phase II awards and total obligations (including obligations on prior awards), as shown in the provided table summarizing agency usage and obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Phase 0 Proof of Concept Partnership (REACH) program purpose and allowable uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized by section 5127 of Public Law 112-81, NIH may use up to $5M of its STTR set-aside to make awards to research institutions (not to exceed $1M per institution per year) to accelerate creation of small businesses and commercialization of research innovations via the REACH program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds may support work including technical validation, market research, clarification of intellectual property rights position and strategy, and investigation of commercial or business opportunities. Agencies should report obligations (e.g., NIH obligated $4,919,457 in FY22) and program outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOE U.S. manufacturing requirement for SBIR/STTR-funded inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE implemented a U.S. competitive provision in SBIR/STTR solicitations beginning in FY2022 requiring that inventions made under SBIR/STTR awards be substantially manufactured in the United States, regardless of where they are later used or sold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provision is implemented pursuant to a Determination of Exceptional Circumstances under the Bayh-Dole Act and DOE Patent Waivers. Agencies adopting similar provisions should describe implementation approach and how the requirement is applied in solicitations and awards.
